To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of diethylzince to aldehydes is catalyzed by chiral cobalt(II) and palladium(II) complexes, and that these catalysts can give optically active aldehydes almost quantitatively with high ee's.
the reaction of diethyl zinc with benzaldehydes catalysed by Co(α-CqdH)2, Pd(α-Cqd-H)2, and Ni(α-Cqd)2 in tolenes at room temperature gives enantiomerically enriched alcohols in high yields.

the reaction of diethyl-zinc with aryl aldehydes in the presence of chiral cobalt and palladium complexes in toluene afforded optically active aliphatic secondary alcohols almost in quantitative yield with high enantiomeric excess.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new chiral catalysts for the enantioselective addition of diethylzine to arylaldehy des.
the synthesis of new chiral cobalt(II) and palladium(II) complexes and the application of these complexes as catalysts for the enantioselective addition of diethylzine to arylaldehyes.
the synthesis of new chiral cobalt complexes and their application to asymmetric catalysis.

the addition of diethylzince to arylaldehyds catalyzed by chiral cobalt(II) and palladium(II) complexes is an efficient method for the preparation of optically active secondary alcohols in high yield.

the reaction is catalyzed by chiral cobalt and palladium complexes, which have a chiral bidentate ligand, α-cqdH (α-cqdH = 2-(2-(2-(1-hydroxyethyl)quinolin-2-yl)ethyl)-4-(2-pyridinyl)-1,3-dioxane).
